gaps: Scope: exported (capitalized) top-level func/type/const/var declarations and exported methods only, extracted via `git grep -nE '^(func|type|const|var) [A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*' -- '*.go'` and `git grep -nE '^func \([^)]+\) [A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*' -- '*.go'`. Unexported identifiers, struct fields, interface method sets declared inline, and package-level init() are excluded.

Reference counting is textual (word-boundary regex via ripgrep, `rg -n -o '\bName\b' -g '*.go'`), not type-checked. For symbol names defined more than once across the codebase (1622 of 4439 records, flagged `name_ambiguous: true` with `distinct_definitions_for_name`), external_refs cannot distinguish which definition a given call site resolves to and is computed against ALL occurrences of that literal name minus the specific definition line being recorded; treat these external_refs numbers as upper-bound estimates only, not precise counts, until disambiguated by a type-aware tool.

external_refs counts raw text matches outside the defining package's directory; it does not itself establish reachability per preamble rule 4. It also cannot see the 9 non-textual mechanisms (interface satisfaction via structural typing, embedding-promoted methods with no direct call site, //go:embed, reflection/string-keyed lookups, JSON tag contracts) except where `registration_sites` (cmd/, routes.go, init_services.go, or path containing 'scheduler') or `build_tags`/`integration_refs` happen to surface them mechanically. Interface satisfaction (mechanism #1) and embedding (mechanism #3) are NOT specifically detected — a method with 0 external_refs may still be live via an interface it satisfies. Downstream consumers must not treat 0 external_refs as proof of dead code without checking these mechanisms independently.

1798 of 4439 records show external_refs == 0. A large fraction of these are expected to be Go test functions (TestXxx, called by the test runtime via reflection, not by other code — mechanism #9) and same-package-only exported helpers. This scout does not classify or judge which zero-ref records are actually dead; that is downstream lens work.
121 records have external references found only in _test.go files (marked test_only: true) — recorded as a distinct usage kind per preamble guidance, not as evidence of being unused.

registration_sites is a mechanical heuristic: any external ref whose file path starts with cmd/, ends with routes.go or init_services.go, or contains the substring 'scheduler' (case-insensitive) anywhere in its path. It is a signal for manual DI-wiring review, not a certified classification.

build_tags reflects only whether the DEFINING file starts with a //go:build integration (or legacy // +build integration) comment in its first 500 bytes; it does not walk build constraints transitively or evaluate other tag combinations.

Method receiver identity uses the raw receiver clause text (e.g. '*Foo' or 'Foo') as written in source, not a resolved type identity; two methods with differently formatted but equivalent receivers (spacing, pointer, generic params) could produce distinct identity strings.
Only default and 'integration' build tags were searched, per instructions; no other tag combinations (none observed elsewhere in the repo) were checked.
